newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude rises as Shell cuts Nigerian output.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude rises as Shell cuts Nigerian output.

text.p: NYMEX crude erased early losses Friday afternoon and posted firm gains on news Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit said ethnic clashes had forced it to close 20 percent of its Forcados crude output.
"It (crude) definitely rose on the Nigeria news, but it has very little impact in the long run since it really is not all that much crude so far," said a New York crude trader.
Still, at 1429 EDT, June crude was 15 cents up at $20.18 a barrel after falling as much as 21 cents to $19.82 early session.
Renewed clashes in the oil-producing swamps between militant youths of Ijaw and Itsekiri tribes in Nigeria forced Shell to close its Warri flow station last weekend.

Traders said the reduction was equivalent to about 90,000 barrels per day of production. But, dealers also noted the state oil company, the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp, said that no cargoes had to be cancelled so far.
Refined products were unable to shake off losses with May heating oil off 0.09 cent a gallon at 55.80 cents and May gasoline off 0.24 cent at 62.60 cents a gallon.

"We are off our highs in crude. We would have to go over $20.25 for it to go much higher," said a New York dealer, noting technical resistance formed by June crude's high for the week. Spot crude failed at resistance, rising to a session high of $20.22.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
